phases.lm_definition: Research, identification and selection of targets.
phases.summary: Opportunistic MaaS targeting; the 2025 Talos campaign chose Ukrainian organisations.
actions: Affiliate picks a target set (Ukrainian entities in the Talos campaign) and lure theme
No victim-specific research documented - commodity loader, volume over precision

phases.name: Weaponization
phases.lm_definition: Coupling a remote access trojan with an exploit into a deliverable payload.
phases.summary: Amadey bought as a service, configured, packed; payloads staged on GitHub and a hijacked GitLab.
actions: Operator develops/sells the Amadey builder + panel (MaaS); affiliate obtains a build
Build config: bot ID 0702f, string-decryption key, encrypted strings; Emmenhtal JS is multi-layer obfuscated
Payloads uploaded to GitHub repos (Legendary99999) and to a compromised self-hosted GitLab
C2 domains registered, incl. brand-impersonating microsoft-telemetry.at

phases.name: Exploitation
phases.lm_definition: Triggering the intruder's code - a vulnerability, or the user/OS auto-executing it.
phases.summary: No software exploit: the user runs the script; Windows script hosts and LOLBins do the rest.
actions: Victim opens the JavaScript from the archive (user execution - the 'exploited' component is the human)
JS -> mshta.exe runs the remote Emmenhtal stage -> PowerShell loads and starts Amadey

phases.name: Installation
phases.lm_definition: Installing a backdoor / persistence on the victim system.
phases.summary: Amadey copies itself to a hex-named folder and survives reboots with a 1-minute scheduled task.
actions: Copies itself to %TEMP%\067640a009\Yfgfwb.exe and starts it (CreateProcess)
Mutex f936986d553273aef6eeaeef713ad28f prevents double infection
Scheduled task Yfgfwb (C:\Windows\Tasks\Yfgfwb.job) runs it every minute
Startup folder redirected in the registry; Zone.Identifier (MotW) zeroed; strings decrypted at runtime

phases.name: Command & Control
phases.lm_definition: Compromised host beacons outbound to an Internet controller.
phases.summary: HTTP POST check-in with an RC4-encrypted host profile; infrastructure shared with StealC.
actions: POST /0gjSy4hf3/index.php to 91.92.243.129 (AS202412) - v5: st=s, then r=<hex(RC4(profile))>
Profile = computer, user, domain, OS, admin rights, AV product, locale check (skips Russia)
Fast-flux DNS for C2 domains; one C2 domain now sinkholed by Microsoft (my Maltego pivot)

phases.lm_definition: The intruder achieves the original goal (theft, destruction, further access).
phases.summary: Plugins steal credentials and swap wallets; the real goal is delivering StealC (next kill chain).
actions: Downloads /0gjSy4hf3/Plugins/clip64.dll; rundll32 ...clip64.dll, Main swaps crypto wallets in the clipboard
cred64.dll steals browser credentials
Pulls StealC (protected.zip) from the hijacked GitLab, PowerShell Expand-Archive, runs x64_protect.exe -> exfil to 158.94.208.130
v5 RAT options: screenshots, SOCKS proxy, RDP + hidden admin + firewall rule; historically LockBit 3.0
